title: OA THE CALENDAR - the twelve months of the Shou Lung calendar with their day counts and festival counts
audit_comment: OA round eighty-three (capture p. 236): the Calendar - the twelve months of the Shou Lung emperor's calendar with their days and the festivals, feasts and holy days counted, single-pass pins per the Chapter 9 provenance shift

banner.title: OA THE CALENDAR, printed capture pp. 236-237 - the months and festivals round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture - the sole surviving pass per the R679 provenance shift. THE CALENDAR: devised in ancient times by one of the great emperors of Shou Lung to fix the regular holidays and festivals, a success used throughout all the civilized lands of Kara-Tur, the first of the year falling sometime in modern-day February or March. THE TWELVE MONTHS with their days and festival counts: Tsou the 30 of eight observances - the New Year's Festival, the God of Heaven, the Feast of Lanterns, the God of Spring, the God of Wealth, the Fertility Festival, the God of Happiness, the God of Learning; Ju the 30 of the God of North and the Goddess of Mercy; Yu the 30 of the God of Central Mound, the Queen of Heaven, the Cherry Blossom Festival; Kao the 30 of the God of Medicine and the God of South; Kao II the 29 of the Thunder God, the Dragon Boat Festival, the God of War; Chu the 30 with none printed; Hsiang the 29 of the God of Fire and the Purification Festival; Chuang the 30 of the Moon Feast Festival, the God of Land and Grain, the God of Furnace, the Great Sage's Birthday; Hsuan the 30 of the Wine God, the Yang Feast, the Polar Gods, the God of Wealth; Yang the 29 of the God of Disease; Ku the 30 with none printed; Tu the 29 of the Kings' Festival. THE YEAR: eight months of 30 days and four of 29 - Kao II, Hsiang, Yang and Tu - the 356-day year. THE OBSERVANCE KINDS: the festivals lasting several days to weeks; the feasts the banquet gatherings; the holy days observed or not per the religion of the area and the character of the inhabitants; the observances simple, the excuse for a feast. The calendar pins per the R431 calculus
